title: surge bust leaks the triggering crit's gold: de-dup guard checks surge.active after recordStrike already busted
description:
Integration seam (app.tsx), invisible to per-PR reviewers. Violates the hkm.3 de-dup contract ('during a surge per-strike eruptions are suppressed; the pot is the only payout') at the overheat-bust seam.

Mechanism: Surge.recordStrike() folds a crit into the pot and then synchronously calls addCoreHeat(critHeatSpike(...)), which calls endSurge('bust') the instant coreTemp crosses critical — flipping _phase to 'idle' (surge.active -> false) inside the same call. Both strike call sites then read that stale-flipped flag:

  - frame loop (src/app.tsx:186-192):  surge.recordStrike(r, baseDamage(s));  if (!surge.active) engine!.erupt(r.damage, r.tier);
  - manualAttack (src/app.tsx:295-303): surge.recordStrike(r, baseDamage(s)); ... if (!surge.active) engineRef.current?.erupt(r.damage, r.tier, target);

Because recordStrike already busted, !surge.active is TRUE for the very crit that triggered the bust, so erupt() fires and deposits that crit's raw damage as collectable world GOLD (depositEruption -> value field -> collector -> essence). Meanwhile bustPot reports the full pot (which includes that same crit) as LOST. Result: every overheat bust leaks the triggering crit's damage back to the player as recoverable gold, contradicting the stated 'you rode it, it pumped, then it burned' contract and the 'pot is the only payout' de-dup invariant. surge.ts:257-264 and its own comment claim the busting crit is 'captured in the pot' and suppressed; the app wiring defeats that.

Only the crit-spike bust path leaks (the ambient tickHeat bust at app.tsx:203 fires outside the results loop, so nothing is being erupted at that moment). Magnitude is bounded to one strike's unmultiplied damage, but it fires on 100% of busts and violates a core conservation/de-dup contract the review targets.

Fix direction: capture whether the surge was active BEFORE recordStrike (const wasActive = surge.active) and gate the erupt on wasActive, or have recordStrike return whether it consumed/suppressed the strike. Not fixing inline per review scope.

Repro: seed a surge, land a crit whose CRIT_SPIKE_BANDS draw pushes coreTemp >= CORE_CRITICAL_TEMP (490) — e.g. a tier-8 crit from cold busts immediately — and observe the triggering strike both counted in the lost pot and deposited as world gold.
close_reason: recordStrike now returns whether the strike was captured by the pot; both erupt call sites key the de-dup guard on that return instead of surge.active, so the crit that busts the surge burns with the pot and never leaks as world gold. regression test added.

title: render the collector drain region on screen

title: eruption gold vanishes at fixed height, never reaches ground
description: playtest report: particles from click eruptions fall, then disappear at the same vertical position well above the terrain — as if hitting an invisible barrier; no gold ever pools on the ground. suspected pixi ballistic phase -> grid handoff: impact y miscomputed (screen-vs-grid coordinate scaling) or handoff writes MOLTEN_GOLD to out-of-bounds/occupied cells that get silently dropped. if cells are dropped, their value is likely vanishing too — check the conservation ledger.
close_reason: root cause: defaultCollectorRegion was a full-width band hugging the terrain surface, so every gold cell was silently drained to essence the moment it settled — read as an invisible barrier. narrowed the default drain to a 40-cell patch centred under the core; gold outside it now pools visibly and stays at risk per design §2.

title: collector fires spurious erase gold-loss event for every collected cell
description: collector.collect (src/game/collector.ts:74) clears drained gold via sim.paint(x,y,0,EMPTY), whose erase branch (simulation.ts:270-273) fires reportGoldLoss(...,'erase') for any gold cell. Every successful collection is therefore double-booked as collected AND lost, breaking the §4.1 ledger sum(value)+collected+lost===erupted, and will mis-fire loss feedback (hiss/flash) at the drain once a listener is attached. Latent because app.tsx attaches no listener yet. Fix: value-zeroing clear that bypasses the erase tell, or exempt collector-cleared cells. Found by wave-3 integration review.

title: eruption landing on solid gold mints value (double-count)
description: depositEruption (src/game/eruption.ts:108) captures prior value before painting, then re-adds it after setCell — but GOLD->MOLTEN_GOLD is a goldPhaseCarry transition, so setCell preserves the value and the re-add DOUBLES it. Verified: GOLD cell value 1000 hit by P=100 eruption ends at totalValue 2100 (expected 1100). Reachable in normal play when a wide eruption lands on settled solid gold; inflates essence. Fix: only re-add prior value when the pre-paint material was MOLTEN_GOLD (the non-carry case). Add a test for eruption-on-solid-gold. Found by wave-3 integration review.

title: per-cell value field with conservation
description: Float32Array parallel to grid, Lagrangian (property of the particle, unlike Eulerian heat). carry contract: swap() moves value with the cell; setCell() zeroes value unless the transition explicitly carries it (GOLD<->MOLTEN_GOLD preserve in place); destruction paths (acid, lava) zero and account as lost. eruption distributes P across cells; INGOT merge consumes neighbor cells + sums value; ingot melt-back spreads value across resulting molten cells (one cell must never carry a whole ingot). invariant test: sum(value field) + collected + lost === total erupted, every frame. design.md §4.1.

title: eruption spawner: pixi ballistic phase -> grid handoff
description: the sim has NO velocity (every cell moves <=1 cell/frame under gravity), so eruption flight is a pixi-layer projectile phase: arcs from core toward cursor with tier-scaled spread, converts to MOLTEN_GOLD grid cells on impact. m = clamp(4 + 6*log10(P), 4, 64); temp table by tier (design.md §6); tier 8 adds lightning + lava spray. design.md §7.

title: MOLTEN_GOLD + GOLD materials

MOLTEN_GOLD needs lava-style heat-carry on movement (heat is Eulerian; without re-seeding the destination cell a flowing stream reads cold and freezes mid-flight — see moveLava). design.md §4.1.
notes: also add INGOT: gold buried under >=N gold neighbors for a few seconds fuses into a static ingot cell worth the merged sum; melts back to molten gold. keeps big wealth visually dense (design.md §4.1).

title: collector catches gold in mid-air above the terrain floor
description:
Found while measuring critstorm-ak0. The collector's catch band reaches 3 rows above the MINIMUM terrain surface and drains every step, so it catches gold before that gold reaches the ground. Any ground-level hazard is therefore irrelevant unless it is filled all the way up to that line — which is why the ak0 bust fix had to pour a level-topped pool rather than scatter fallout.

Consequence: in a terrain dip the pool falls short of the catch line and the hazard leaks. Measured during ak0 development: one strike column still returned 84% of its clean take because the pool sat below the band there.

Owner: src/game/collector.ts (region geometry). Left untouched by ak0, which fenced to bust.ts.
acceptance_criteria: the catch band's relationship to local terrain height is specified and implemented deliberately; a ground-level hazard under the drain cannot be bypassed by gold being caught above it

title: [bug] heat-realism test uses unseeded Math.random and flakes
description:
src/sim/heat-realism.test.ts > 'a fire body submerged in water is quenched quickly' uses unseeded Math.random, violating the repo's determinism convention (CLAUDE.md: anything random takes a seeded rng and must be unit-testable).

Observed failing once in a full-suite run during wave 8, passing 3x in isolation and in 4 later full runs. A blind verifier independently saw '1 failed | 425 passed' at baseline 3a6e5aa with two immediate re-runs green; that run's failing test name was not captured, so identifying it as this same test is inference rather than proof.

Fix: thread a seeded rng through the test the way the rest of the suite does (see sim/rng.ts withSeededRandom, used in src/game/bust.test.ts).
acceptance_criteria: the test takes a seeded rng and produces identical results across runs; 20 consecutive full-suite runs green

title: re-specify the overclock deficit-closure metric
description:
critstorm-5xo refuted the 90% deficit-closure floor on holdout: 24/24 disjoint cohorts below it, median -0.107 against a tuning value of 0.9036. The constants are not the problem — a 4x3 grid over OVERCLOCK_FACTOR_PER_STACK and OVERCLOCK_SURGE_HEAT_SHARE lifted no holdout cohort above 0.09, and the tuning cohort swings 0.9036 -> 0.361 -> 0.328 -> -0.164 across those settings (chaotic response, not insensitivity).

Root cause is the estimator. deficitClosed = (overclock - baseline) / (noTurret - baseline) divides one small difference of medians by another, where each arm's cores/min has a standard deviation about 1.5x its own median (compounding growth gives heavy tails). It flips sign in 15 of 24 cohorts. A 0.10-wide band against sigma=0.27 is unsatisfiable at n=129 for any constants.

The measurement harness now exists: sim/overclock-holdout.ts, sim/overclock-holdout-sweep.ts. Candidate replacements noted in .orchestra/scratch/5xo-holdout-results.md section 5: log-scale ratio, paired per-seed median, paired sign test. Pick one, define the floor against it, and restore a real assertion.
acceptance_criteria: a metric whose sampling distribution supports the assertion at the cohort sizes actually run; a floor defined against it and justified by design intent; sim/storm-bot.test.ts asserts that floor rather than pinning the tuning-cohort value
notes: sim/storm-bot.test.ts:352 currently pins toBeCloseTo(0.903656, 6) and toBeCloseTo(0.966987, 6) as explicitly non-generalising tuning-cohort pins. The ceiling guardrail overclock35 < noTurret35 does hold on holdout and remains a real assertion. Blocking risk flagged by the verifier: if a future change moves closure to 0.4, the pin fails and someone may simply re-pin it, with nothing in the suite objecting.

title: bust lava is spatially inert: it pools where the gold route never goes
description:
playtest: on an overheat bust, lava drops from the core and gathers under the middle pipe. the player kept striking above the collector and gold kept collecting normally — the lava never touched the gold route, so the bust had no ongoing physical cost beyond losing the pot.

the mechanic itself works: lava absorbs MOLTEN_GOLD on contact and books the loss (src/sim/simulation.ts:1095 hasLavaNeighbor, :1262 molten-gold consumption, GoldLossCause 'lava' at :98). the problem is placement — if bust lava reliably settles somewhere the player's chosen eruption arc does not cross, the punishment is decorative.

design intent (§3) is that an overheat bust erupts the pot as lava and fire and melts nearby world gold, i.e. the aftermath should keep pressuring the player. right now the aftermath can be ignored by continuing to click in the same spot.
acceptance_criteria: a bust leaves a hazard the player must route around or clear; striking the same collector-adjacent spot after a bust is measurably worse than before it (harness or focused test showing post-bust collection loss or forced repositioning).
close_reason: bust fallout now pours as a level-topped pool across the drain approach. shipping-geometry measurement: dx=0 collects 2022/18000 (11%) post-bust vs 18000 (100%) clean; flanks stay workable (dx=16 banks 93% of its clean take) so repositioning is the out. value conservation exact; blind-verified (same model, independent context) PASS_WITH_NOTES, all 4 notes fixed.

title: sim event seams for audio: gold-settle + phase-change listeners
description: sh8.2's synth layer shipped engine-ready methods (quench/ignite/goldLand) that have nothing to subscribe to: simulation.ts only exposes setGoldLossListener. add a GoldSettleEvent {x,y,amount} listener (MOLTEN_GOLD→GOLD, updateMoltenGold ~1276) and one phase-change listener with a kind discriminator (boil|quench|ignite) covering updateWater ~972, updateLava crust ~1142, and the ignition gates ~832-880. mirror the gold-loss seam pattern. then wire quench/ignite/goldLand call sites.
close_reason: GoldSettleEvent + PhaseChangeEvent(boil|quench|ignite) seams added to simulation.ts mirroring the gold-loss seam; bridged to the synth via SimLayer.attachAudio, attached at app.tsx:372 and released on storm teardown. blind-verified PASS on all 5 criteria (same model, independent context).

title: first-run legibility: the loop is not explained anywhere in-game
description:
playtest feedback: the game reads as interesting but the mechanics are not legible on a first run. there is currently no onboarding surface at all — no tutorial, no first-run prompts, and only two hover titles in the whole UI (src/app.tsx:820 and :827 on the crit histogram). design.md has no onboarding section; it assumes teaching happens by playing (the flats as tutorial front, §4.5 line 145, and the first-storm blow-up as a teaching moment, §6 line 183), which is not enough on its own.

this is distinct from the sh8 presentation epic: sh8.1 is art direction, sh8.2 audio, sh8.3 juice on bank/bust. none of them teach what to click or why. scope needs deciding — candidates are surge/bank-or-ride legibility, what heat and the strike do, why to paint defense, and what cores/workshop are for.
notes:
new scope not covered by design.md; needs a design decision on how much explicit teaching v1 wants before implementing.

PLAYTEST BRAINDUMP (2026-08-14, first real session by the owner):

premise — someone with zero context does not know what the game is about at all. this is the top-level gap; everything below is a symptom.

workshop — reads as a between-rounds shop, but the nodes do not say what they mean. tooltips on the workshop nodes explaining the effect in plain terms would help.

materials — the world quietly gains water, lava and glass mid-storm with no acknowledgement. player notices new pixel colours and has no idea what changed or why.

sidebar copy is circular — the WATER brush says 'quenches molten gold fast', but nothing has told the player what molten gold is, where it comes from, or why quenching it is good or bad (it is both: §4.2, solid gold does not flow to the collector).

surge — guessable as 'bonus points, bank in time or bust', but what busting actually costs is not communicated. the pot is the unbanked value and a bust erupts it as lava and fire (§3), and none of that reads.

lava is inert in practice — on bust, lava drops from the core and gathers under the middle pipe. the player kept clicking above the pipe and gold kept collecting normally. mechanically lava does absorb MOLTEN_GOLD on contact (src/sim/simulation.ts:1095, :1262), but if bust lava always pools where the gold route never goes, the punishment never lands. that is a spatial/balance problem, not a copy problem — likely wants its own issue.

storm events — acid drizzle and lightning fronts arrive with no telegraph or label. they look cool but read as 'wtf just happened'.

title: holdout-cohort validation for the auto-striker overclock tuning
description: the overclock deficit-closure margin was tuned to 90.36% against a 90% floor on a 129-seed median curve. the margin is thin and the seeds used for tuning are the seeds used for the assertion, so the result may be overfit. per-storm variance around the median was never characterised. run a fresh holdout seed cohort and report the distribution, not just the median.
acceptance_criteria: holdout cohort distinct from the tuning seeds reported with median and spread; the 90% floor either holds or the constants are retuned
close_reason: holdout run and reported; the 90% floor is REFUTED, not validated. 3096 fresh seeds in 24 cohorts, provably disjoint from the tuning set by range: median -0.106538, stddev 0.270289, min -0.911, max 0.345, 24/24 cohorts below the floor. The tuning value 0.9036 sits +3.8 sigma above the holdout mean. Independently reproduced digit-for-digit by a blind verifier, which also showed a cohort sharing 128 of 129 seeds with the tuning set scores 0.835 — so 0.9036 is a property of that exact seed list. Constants left unchanged deliberately: a 4x3 grid over OVERCLOCK_FACTOR_PER_STACK and OVERCLOCK_SURGE_HEAT_SHARE lifted no holdout cohort above 0.09. Fixing this means re-specifying the metric, filed separately.

WHAT REMAINS IS A DESIGN DECISION, NOT A BUG. design.md:180 describes Aegis as 'defense brushes unlocked from storm start' — an unlock model the code never implemented, having shipped cost multipliers instead. That line is what led the wave-6b reviewer to look for unlock nodes. Either implement the unlock model or amend design.md to match the shipped cost model. Needs a human call; left open for it.

title: harness cannot measure §8 pacing gates: time-to-first-surge and brush affordability
description: wave-5b finding: the storm harness has no click->heat-fill model (surge harness ignites instantly) and no brush/paint purchase model, so 'first surge within ~90s' and 'first brush affordable ~90s in' (design §8) are unmeasurable and untuned. extend the harness with a click-cadence bot and the brush cost model, then assert both gates.
design: Use a deterministic 2.5 clicks/sec reference bot at fixed timestep; one complete unobstructed radius-3 stone stroke is the affordability unit and painting consumes one scheduled pointer action. Land before critstorm-3il rebaseline.
acceptance_criteria: Headless harness drives real manual click cadence through executeStrike and Surge, records actual first-surge ignition and first complete stone-brush stroke, preserves deterministic RNG/accounting and dt scaling, and asserts the design §8 timing bands with focused and full green gates.

title: late-storm essence compounding lever: cores/min flattens past ~30 min
description: wave-5b harness finding: constants alone cannot hold the design §6 pace late — median essence growth is x8.6 (10-20min) but x3.4 (20-30min), and cores/min plateaus past ~30 min because critMulti under geometric cost is the only sustained in-storm lever (~quadratic essence vs sqrt cores). the coarse-arc anti-farming guarantee is pinned, but the 25-35 min endgame needs a new compounding mechanic — collection-efficiency scaling, structures (magnet/auto-striker synergy), or a meta multiplier. mechanics work, belongs with the gen/j5g epics.
acceptance_criteria: After critstorm-iby lands, rebaseline the realistic competent bot across deterministic seeds. Median essence growth must stay within x5-x20 for 20-30m and 25-35m, coarse cores/min marks 8/15/22/29/35 must rise by at least 5%, and 35m cores/min must exceed 30m by at least 15%. Prove the existing auto-striker causally improves the curve via an ablation; if it already passes, close as measurement hardening without inventing another mechanic.
notes: The original plateau evidence is stale at baseline f2dddf4: current synthetic sweep already rises past 30m. Do not add a speculative multiplier before the realistic critstorm-iby harness rebaseline.

title: bust severity swings 1%-79% on terrain seed alone
description:
Raised by the critstorm-ak0 blind verifier as a balance observation, not a defect. Measuring post-bust collection at the same strike column across 7 terrain seeds in shipping geometry gave 1%, 8%, 67%, 50%, 26%, 79%, 48% of a clean run.

One terrain seed costs the player almost everything; another barely stings. Nothing is broken: the fun-floor holds (pressure lasts ~30s at SIM_STEP_SEC=0.05, always recovers unaided, water brush quenches — lava 70 -> 21 cells in 400 steps), and no soft-lock was found across edge cases including core at grid edges, packed grid, 1x1 grid, and pot 1e12.

The question is whether a punishment that varies this widely on terrain alone is the intended feel (design 2 fun-floor, design 3 bust). If not, the fallout placement wants to adapt to local terrain rather than filling to a fixed rise.
acceptance_criteria: a decision recorded on whether this spread is intended; if not, fallout placement adapted so bust severity is comparable across terrain seeds

title: chain-detonated gunpowder emits no ignite event
description:
The phase-change seam added in critstorm-f1d hooks the four ignition gates in updateLava/heat paths (simulation.ts ~:916 gunpowder, :928 oil, :954 wood, :961 plant). Gunpowder lit by a neighbouring blast inside explode() bypasses those gates entirely, so a chain detonation produces no ignite event and therefore no audio.

Raised by the f1d blind verifier. Explicitly outside f1d's stated scope (the ticket named the ignition gates), so it was not treated as a defect there.
acceptance_criteria: chain detonation inside explode() emits ignite phase-change events consistent with the heat-gate path; covered by a test

title: repair and harden codex wave runner recovery
description: Wave 6a exposed recovery and runtime-contract failures in the Codex wave runner: REVIEW_SCHEMA declares optional findings.line, but strict structured-output validation requires every property to be listed in required; failed npm ci can leave a partial node_modules that makes npx attempt a network install; failed pipelines retain claimed beads state, branches, PRs, and worktrees but the runner has no resume mode; and a capacity failure forces whole-wave manual recovery. Harden the runner so future waves fail predictably and can resume without reimplementing completed tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Review output schema is valid under the current Codex structured-output contract and covered by a real validation test; dependency setup failures cannot leave a misleading partial install used by gates; a documented resume/recovery path reuses completed PRs and retained worktrees safely; failed task state and beads claims are reported clearly; runner tests and TypeScript pass.
close_reason: codex wave runner deleted; waves now run via native collaboration subagents

Defaults are safe and the bounds test only exercises defaults — clamp and add a non-default test.
